verdict: DISCIPLINED PROGRAMMATIC ISSUER — A REVOLVING PIPE, REFILLED ON SCHEDULE
lead: Welltower runs the ATM as a standing capital-markets machine, not an emergency valve: eleven programs since 2019 and $32.6B sold — roughly 280M shares, about half of today’s share count — at a blended $115.49, with realized prices stepping from the $70s to the $240s as the program scaled. The pipe was just reloaded: a fresh $7.5B shelf filed July 28, 2026, good for about three quarters at the ~$2.4B/quarter pace, in line with the ~6–7-month refill habit and each refill larger than the last ($2B → $7.5B). Officer and director open-market activity is five prints in seven years against $2–4B of issuance per quarter: the dilution decision is treasury policy, not insiders cashing out through the company.
capacity_read: The reservoir never runs dry: retired shelves are used to ~77% (median) and replaced before exhaustion. Treat “remaining capacity” as a revolving figure, not a ceiling — the constraint on future issuance is appetite and cost of equity, not authorization.
footer_extra: Welltower reports most ATM activity in periodic filings, so sales since the last covered filing (July 28, 2026) are not yet public.
